standard.title: Mathematical Modelling with Ratios
standard.description: use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving ratios; formulate problems, interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation, justifying choices made about the representation
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can recognise, represent and solve ratio problems (from AC9M7N08). Students have used mathematical modelling in numerical contexts (from AC9M7N09).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use mathematical modelling to formulate and solve practical problems involving ratios of measurement quantities, communicating and justifying solutions in context.

nodes.label: Recognising ratio structure in measurement problems
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students identify when a practical measurement problem involves a ratio relationship and represent it using ratio notation.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the ratio relationship in a given practical measurement problem (e.g. mixing paint, scaling a recipe) and write it in a:b form.
nodes.typical_width: Distinguish part-part and part-whole ratio structures in measurement problems; represent both using diagrams and notation.
wider: Investigate ratio applications in scale drawings and maps — connect scale ratios to measurement.
Explore ratio in construction and design contexts: concrete mix ratios, fertiliser dilution rates.

response_modes.reason: Ratio problems in measurement span a wider variety of contexts than number strand ratio problems — scale, mix, division of space — and students need exposure to multiple contexts to recognise the common structure.

success_criteria: Correctly identifies the ratio structure in a practical measurement problem.
Represents the ratio using appropriate notation.
Distinguishes part-part from part-whole ratio in context.

nodes.label: Formulating, solving and interpreting ratio models
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students formulate a ratio model for a practical measurement problem, solve it, and interpret and communicate the solution in terms of the original situation.
nodes.minimum_width: Formulate and solve a practical ratio problem (e.g. mixing liquids, dividing a length) and express the answer with appropriate units.
nodes.typical_width: Solve multi-step ratio problems in measurement contexts; justify representation choices; check reasonableness.
wider: Investigate First Nations Australians' applications of ratio in substances and land use — formulate and solve a contextualised ratio problem.
Model a design problem where a ratio constraint must be satisfied (e.g. designing a scale model at 1:50 ratio).

response_modes.reason: Formulating, solving and communicating a ratio model requires simultaneous application of ratio understanding, measurement, unit reasoning, and modelling conventions. This integration is the core learning.

success_criteria: Formulates the ratio model correctly from the problem description.
Solves the problem and expresses the answer with appropriate measurement units.
Justifies the representation choice and checks the solution for reasonableness.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations contexts and scale model design offer advancing students genuine modelling richness — the ratio constraint in a design problem requires coordinating measurement, ratio, and communication simultaneously.
